The rules for '''[[persona]]s''' decide which cards count as the same character, starship, vehicle, weapon or device, so that a player can't have two versions of one character on the table at once. Decipher introduced personas in [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] (1997) and wrote the core rules into its Glossary; the [[Players Committee]] later widened them to cover Virtual cards, more card types and new characters.<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009141805/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="gl20">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Star Wars Customizable Card Game Glossary, Version 2.0], Decipher (November 1998), entries "personas", "persona replacement rule" and "crossing over". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081221001241/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Decipher Glossary 2.0]]</ref>

== Decipher era ==
=== Hoth (1997) ===
The persona mechanic arrived with [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]], whose [[Commander Luke Skywalker]] was a second card for the character already printed as [[Luke Skywalker]] in Premiere.<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009141805/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]</ref>

=== Glossary 2.0 (1998) ===
Decipher's Glossary Version 2.0 (November 1998) set out the rule: different versions of a single character are part of the same persona, and no more than one version of the same unique persona may be on table at the same time. Cards that name "Luke" apply to every version of the Luke persona (Luke Skywalker, Commander Luke Skywalker, Son of Skywalker), and "Chewbacca" and "Chewie" are interchangeable.<ref name="gl20">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Star Wars Customizable Card Game Glossary, Version 2.0], Decipher (November 1998), entries "personas", "persona replacement rule" and "crossing over". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081221001241/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Decipher Glossary 2.0]]</ref>

The Glossary also introduced the '''persona replacement rule'''. During your deploy phase you may replace one of your characters on table with another version of the same persona from your hand, for free, if the new version has power and ability at least equal to the replaced card's and obeys its own deployment restrictions. Its example: Luke Skywalker (power 3, ability 4) may be replaced by Commander Luke Skywalker (power 4, ability 4), but only on Hoth, because Commander Luke Skywalker deploys only on Hoth. Weapons, devices and Effects on the old version move to the new one if they still apply; the rest go to the Lost Pile with the replaced card. Different versions are still different cards, so [[Grimtaash]], which looks for duplicate cards, does not treat a Luke Skywalker and a Commander Luke Skywalker as two of the same.<ref name="gl20">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Star Wars Customizable Card Game Glossary, Version 2.0], Decipher (November 1998), entries "personas", "persona replacement rule" and "crossing over". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081221001241/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Decipher Glossary 2.0]]</ref>

'''Crossing over''' was defined in the same Glossary. A character who "gives in" to the other side of the Force through [[Epic Duel]] moves to the other player's side and conceptually takes on a new identity, as Anakin Skywalker became Darth Vader; the opponent may not deploy that persona again for the rest of the game.<ref name="gl20">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Star Wars Customizable Card Game Glossary, Version 2.0], Decipher (November 1998), entries "personas", "persona replacement rule" and "crossing over". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081221001241/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Decipher Glossary 2.0]]</ref>

=== Starships, permanent pilots and the Emperor ===
Combination cards carry more than one persona. [[Death Star Assault Squadron]] includes the personas of Darth Vader, DS-61-2, DS-61-3, Vader's Custom TIE, Black 2 and Black 3, and when a unique card is placed out of play, every persona on that card, including starship and permanent pilot personas, may not be deployed again that game.<ref name="gl20">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Star Wars Customizable Card Game Glossary, Version 2.0], Decipher (November 1998), entries "personas", "persona replacement rule" and "crossing over". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081221001241/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Decipher Glossary 2.0]]</ref>

Decipher's Glossary Supplement (2002) kept three separate characters apart: Darth Sidious, Senator Palpatine and Emperor Palpatine were three distinct personas, "unrelated to each other for all game play purposes", referred to as Sidious, Palpatine and Emperor.<ref name="glsupp">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossarysupplement.pdf Star Wars CCG Glossary Supplement], Decipher (updated 29 January 2002), entry "Darth Sidious". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20081221001241/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossarysupplement.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Decipher Glossary Supplement]]</ref>

== Players Committee ==
=== Advanced Rulebook 2.0 (2013) ===
The Players Committee's Advanced Rulebook 2.0 defined a persona as the different versions of a single character, starship or weapon, "even if they are on different sides of the Force". Any card that targets a persona may target any card that contains it, so [[Lando In Millennium Falcon]] counts as Lando; but only character cards may persona replace, and cards that deploy on a character persona must still deploy on a character card.<ref name="ar20">[http://www.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/ar_version-2-0_final.pdf Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 2.0], starwarsccg.org (2013), Chapter 5, "Persona" and "Persona Replacement". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20150807023558/http://www.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/ar_version-2-0_final.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 2.0]]</ref>

It also defined '''different versions''' for persona replacement: two cards are different versions if their titles differ, or if one has an expansion icon the other lacks. That let a Virtual card replace the Decipher card it reworked, for example [[Commander Luke Skywalker (V)]] replacing [[Commander Luke Skywalker]]. Cards with exactly the same title are the same persona (for example [[Laudica]] and its Virtual version).<ref name="ar20">[http://www.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/ar_version-2-0_final.pdf Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 2.0], starwarsccg.org (2013), Chapter 5, "Persona" and "Persona Replacement". Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20150807023558/http://www.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2013/04/ar_version-2-0_final.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook 2.0]]</ref>

=== Advanced Rulebook (2023) ===
The current Advanced Rulebook extends the persona rule to unique devices and vehicles as well as characters, starships and weapons. Each player may have their own version of a unique persona on table at the same time (each player may have a Lando), but not two cards with the same title, and two exceptions apply to captives and stolen cards.<ref name="ar2023">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Players Committee Advanced Rulebook] (2023), Chapter 5 ("Persona", "Persona Replacement", "Persona - Converting Characters", "Persona - Crossing Over", Table 5-1) and Appendix D ("Persona Lists"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192915/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]]</ref>

It also changed the Emperor: "All of his cards share the same persona, his true identity — 'Sidious'." Text that names Palpatine or Emperor refers to the Sidious cards with that word in their title.<ref name="ar2023">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Players Committee Advanced Rulebook] (2023), Chapter 5 ("Persona", "Persona Replacement", "Persona - Converting Characters", "Persona - Crossing Over", Table 5-1) and Appendix D ("Persona Lists"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192915/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]]</ref> Anakin Skywalker and Darth Vader, by contrast, are two people for game purposes and may both be on table; if both are and one crosses over, the player who now owns both must choose one to be lost.<ref name="ar2023">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Players Committee Advanced Rulebook] (2023), Chapter 5 ("Persona", "Persona Replacement", "Persona - Converting Characters", "Persona - Crossing Over", Table 5-1) and Appendix D ("Persona Lists"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192915/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]]</ref>

Crossing over now changes a card's owner, allegiance icons, persona name and card title, following Table 5-1: Anakin Skywalker becomes Vader, Leia becomes Lady Vader, Luke becomes Son Of Vader and Ben Solo becomes Kylo.<ref name="ar2023">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Players Committee Advanced Rulebook] (2023), Chapter 5 ("Persona", "Persona Replacement", "Persona - Converting Characters", "Persona - Crossing Over", Table 5-1) and Appendix D ("Persona Lists"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192915/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]]</ref> Converting (for example Dark Side Lando Calrissian being "replaced" by a Light Side Lando, or [[Double Agent]] on the [[Tonnika Sisters]]) is a change of loyalty, not persona replacement.<ref name="ar2023">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Players Committee Advanced Rulebook] (2023), Chapter 5 ("Persona", "Persona Replacement", "Persona - Converting Characters", "Persona - Crossing Over", Table 5-1) and Appendix D ("Persona Lists"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192915/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]]</ref>

Appendix D lists the standard persona names, including starship personas (Executor, the Falcon, Slave I, Vader's Custom TIE), weapon personas (Vader's Lightsaber, Qui-Gon's Lightsaber, Maul's Lightsaber, Ahsoka's and Asajj's lightsabers) and character personas, plus the non-unique names "Skywalker" and "Fett".<ref name="ar2023">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Players Committee Advanced Rulebook] (2023), Chapter 5 ("Persona", "Persona Replacement", "Persona - Converting Characters", "Persona - Crossing Over", Table 5-1) and Appendix D ("Persona Lists"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192915/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Internet Archive]. Wiki transcription: [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook]]</ref>
